t.E943b.agn: In 2025 EFSA re-evaluated the three together: it stated that the known effects via inhalation are not relevant to the food additive assessment, that dietary exposure is very low and that there is no safety concern at the authorised uses. EFSA noted that the current specifications contain a limit for 1,3-butadiene, but that uncertainty remains about other impurities owing to a lack of information on manufacturing processes, and recommended that the specifications be updated.
t.E943b.found.0: Vegetable oil pan sprays (for professional use only)
t.E943b.found.2: Food colour preparations (maximum 1 mg/kg residue in the food)
t.E943b.prod: Obtained from natural gas by physical separation (fractionation).
t.E943b.regx.0: Re-evaluated together with butane and propane; no safety concern at the authorised uses; updating of the specifications (impurities) recommended.
t.E943b.regx.1: Propellant only in vegetable oil pan spray (professional use) and water-based emulsion spray; in colour preparations, maximum 1 mg/kg residue in the food.
t.E943b.summary: A gas used to replace air in packaging or as a propellant. It prevents the product from oxidising or allows it to be dispensed from spray containers.
t.E943b.what: A short-chain hydrocarbon (isobutane) used as a propellant in oil and emulsion sprays.
